construct: Account-level balancing proof compares two figures carried at different precisions and applies a one-sided tolerance wide enough to absorb the difference
description: CABBIL11 is the control that says an invoice is internally consistent before it is numbered and printed. It builds the detail side in P3100-ACCUM-LINE by adding BD-TOT-ROUNDED, the two decimal place figure CABBIL02 produced with COMPUTE ... ROUNDED in P4500-ROUND-GROUP. It takes the header side in P5100-LOAD-COMPARE from BH-HASH-AMOUNT, which CABBIL09 populated in P4200-POST-TOTALS by accumulating BD-TOT-AMOUNT, the unrounded five decimal place figure. The two sides therefore differ by the accumulated rounding residue of every detail line on the account, which CABBIL02 already computes and carries on the record as BD-ROUND-DELTA. P5200-COMPARE-TOTALS then evaluates COMPUTE WS-DIFF = WS-CW-HDR-AMOUNT - WS-CW-DTL-AMOUNT and tests IF WS-DIFF > WS-CW-TOLERANCE, where WS-CW-TOLERANCE is 0.05. The test is one-sided as well as too wide: a negative difference of any size passes, because a negative value is never greater than 0.05. An account whose detail sums low by a dollar is reported IN BALANCE. The five cent tolerance was introduced in V2.00 in 2001 with the comment that the zero tolerance test was failing large accounts every cycle - it was, and the reason it was failing them is the precision mismatch, which the tolerance hid rather than fixed. CABBIL11 also accumulates WS-DS-DELTA-SUM from BD-ROUND-DELTA and writes it onto the proof record, so the evidence that the two sides cannot agree is on the file the balancing report reads.
business_impact: The estate's own account-level money control does not work. Every invoice is reported as internally consistent whatever the rounding residue, and every invoice whose detail sums LOW is reported as consistent whatever the size of the shortfall. CABRPT01 consumes the proof file and repeats the verdict, and the verdict line on the last page of the daily balancing report is what operations read before releasing the print stream. A modernization programme that treats the existing control as a working parity oracle will certify a rewrite as correct on the strength of a check that cannot fail. On a real estate the exposure is the difference between what the detail pages of a bill add up to and what the summary page and the receivable say - a difference the carrier's own receivables system will find.
correct_modernization_response: Do not carry the two sides at different precisions. Either accumulate the header control figure from the same rounded line totals the detail side uses, or carry the detail side unrounded and compare like with like, and in both cases account for the residue explicitly rather than absorbing it in a tolerance. Make the comparison two-sided by taking the absolute difference. Reduce the tolerance to zero and, if a tolerance is genuinely required for a business reason, express it as a documented parameter with the reason recorded, not as a literal in working storage. In a target-state rewrite use a decimal type with a declared scale end to end and one rounding point per money field, and reconcile BD-ROUND-DELTA into a residue account so the penny is posted rather than tolerated. Before any of that, re-run the existing control with the tolerance set to zero and an absolute difference to establish how many accounts are actually out of balance today - that number is the true baseline for a parity test.

construct: Carriage control character and its associated counter are set before the condition that governs them is tested, and the invoice break already counts the section it opens
description: In CABSPRNT the character in column one carries business meaning as well as printer positioning: '7' is start of a new invoice to the burst and insert machinery, '4' is start of a new bill section. P3100-START-INVOICE writes the invoice header line with '7' and, correctly, treats that break as opening the first section by executing ADD 1 TO WS-PG-SECTION-CNT. It then clears WS-PG-PRIOR-SECTION to spaces. P3300-ASSIGN-CARRIAGE-CONTROL is entered for the first detail line of that invoice and begins with MOVE '4' TO PC-CC followed by ADD 1 TO WS-PG-SECTION-CNT, before it tests IF BD-SECTION = WS-PG-PRIOR-SECTION. Because the prior section was cleared at the invoice break the comparison is always unequal on the first detail line, so neither the character nor the increment is backed out. Every invoice therefore emits a '4' immediately after its '7' and counts two sections where one has started. The count is moved to WS-PR-SECTIONS in P4000-CLOSE-INVOICE and written to TELCABS.CABS.PRTCTL, the file the burst process and the mailroom reconcile against, and CABFMT08 independently counts the '4' characters in the finished stream and arrives at the same inflated figure, so the two sources agree with each other and disagree with reality.
business_impact: Cosmetic on paper - an extra skip to channel four at the top of a bill is invisible to the reader. Not cosmetic downstream: the burst process counts sections to decide where to fold and the mailroom reconciles the section count against the number of folds the burster made. Every invoice reports one section too many, so the reconciliation is out by exactly the number of invoices in the run and has been for as long as the discrepancy has been tolerated. Any modernization that reimplements the print stream from the printed output will reproduce the extra break; any that reimplements it from the specification will produce a section count that no longer matches the legacy control file, and the difference will look like a regression in the new system rather than a defect in the old one.
correct_modernization_response: Assign the carriage control character and increment the section counter only after the section-change condition has been evaluated, and treat the invoice break as opening the first section rather than counting it twice. In a target-state rewrite separate the two meanings the character is carrying: emit a document model with explicit invoice and section boundaries, render the printer control from that model, and let the burst and insert instructions come from the same model rather than from a character that has to mean two things at once. Establish the correct section count before migration and expect the legacy print control file to be one high per invoice - that offset is a known-difference, not a parity failure.

construct: The pre-bill audit is run against a total that excludes the adjustment and restatement components, and those components are added back only after the audit has finished
description: CABBIL10 does not trust the total due that arrives on the header - the record has been through four steps since it was last totalled - so P2300-RECOMPUTE-TOTAL rebuilds BH-TOTAL-DUE from its components. The rebuild adds prior balance, payments, the three current period fields, the settlement net and the tax, and omits BH-ADJUSTMENTS and BH-RESTATEMENT. P2400-SET-AUDIT-BASIS moves that figure into WS-HB-BASIS. The whole of the pre-bill audit then runs against WS-HB-BASIS: P3100-HOLD-TEST-NEGATIVE tests it for a negative invoice, P3200-HOLD-TEST-VARIANCE computes the bill-to-bill movement from it, and P3500-HOLD-TEST-LIMIT tests it against the delegated authority limit. Only after P3000-PREBILL-AUDIT has returned does P3600-APPLY-ADJ-TO-TOTAL execute COMPUTE BH-TOTAL-DUE = BH-TOTAL-DUE + BH-ADJUSTMENTS + BH-RESTATEMENT. An account whose current charges are positive but which carries a credit adjustment or a negative factor restatement large enough to take the invoice below zero therefore passes every hold test and is written out with status P, is numbered by CABBIL12, and is printed and mailed as a negative invoice. The comment on P3600 offers a plausible reason for holding the adjustment out of the recomputation - so that the three current period fields can be proved against the detail - and that reason is true of the recomputation; it is not a reason for running the audit against the incomplete figure.
business_impact: The control that stops a refund leaving the building without a human looking at it does not fire for the single most common way an invoice becomes negative. A large credit adjustment or a retroactive PIU restatement in the carrier's favour produces a negative invoice that is numbered, printed and sent. The carrier receives what looks like a demand for a negative amount; their receivables system either rejects the whole interchange or posts a credit the accounts receivable ledger was not expecting. The variance and delegated authority tests are affected in the same way and for the same reason: a bill that moved by five hundred per cent because of an adjustment is measured on the pre-adjustment figure and passes. The hold reason HNEG exists, is on the hold reason master, and has a counter that is reported every cycle - and it only ever fires for accounts that were already negative before adjustment, which is rare.
correct_modernization_response: Apply the adjustment and restatement components before the audit runs, or run the audit against a separately derived final total. If the recomputation genuinely needs a pre-adjustment figure to prove the current period fields against the detail, derive two values - a detail-proof basis and an audit basis - and name them so that the difference is explicit. In a target-state rewrite the invoice total should be a single derived value computed once from a complete set of components, and the pre-bill audit should be a rule set that runs against the finished invoice, not against an intermediate. When migrating, re-run the historical hold decisions against the corrected basis to size the population of negative invoices that were released - that population is a real financial exposure and needs to be quantified before the corrected logic goes live, because it will start holding bills that used to go out.

construct: The fixed-width image a program builds for its own internal SORT is narrower than the variable-length record it is imaging, so the ordering step discards the tail of every long record and hands back storage that record does not own, while the length field that governs the write survives intact
description:
CABBIL03 puts the bill detail into print order using a COBOL SORT held inside the program - the ordering step is invisible from the JCL and from every sort control card in the estate. The record it orders is CABSBILL, whose length is governed by BD-ELEM-CNT: a 127-byte fixed portion followed by one to forty rate elements of 38 bytes each. Add those up and the longest possible detail record is 127 + 40 x 38 = 1,647 data bytes, which is LRECL 1651 once the RDW is counted, and it is what both FD clauses in this program now declare - each one varying from 108 to 1647 characters, governed by BD-ELEM-CNT.

The SD does not agree with them. SORT-RECORD is a flat 1,232 bytes: a 28-byte four-part key of BAN, bill period, section print order and line sequence, followed by SR-IMAGE PIC X(1204). The two halves of the round trip are one statement each. P4300-BUILD-SORT-REC executes MOVE CABS-BILL-DETAIL TO SR-IMAGE, so a detail record longer than 1,204 bytes loses its tail on the way in. P5200-RETURN-ONE executes MOVE SR-IMAGE TO CABS-BILL-DETAIL, so only what the image held comes back out.

The arithmetic fixes where the cut falls, and it is worth doing rather than assuming. 1,204 minus the 127-byte fixed portion leaves 1,077 bytes of element space. 1,077 divided by 38 is 28 with 13 left over. Twenty-eight elements therefore survive whole, occupying bytes 128 through 1,191. The 13 bytes left over hold the front of the twenty-ninth element - its six-byte BD-EL-RATE-ELEM and seven of the eight bytes of its packed BD-EL-QTY - so even the element that straddles the cut comes back with a quantity that has lost its low-order digit and its sign nibble and is no longer valid packed decimal. Elements thirty through forty were never in the image at all. The last position that is reliably the record's own is 28.

BD-ELEM-CNT sits at bytes 125 through 127, inside the fixed portion, so it makes the round trip untouched. P5400-WRITE-SEQUENCED clamps it to the range one to forty, which a genuine count of twenty-nine to forty passes without comment, and writes the record through an FD whose length is governed by that same count. The record therefore leaves the program at its full claimed length with positions twenty-nine onward filled from whatever occupies that storage.

What occupies it is the whole point. CABS-BILL-DETAIL is not working storage - it is the record area of BILL-DTL-IN, brought in by COPY CABSBILL directly under that FD, and that file is not closed until P9000-TERM. This program is outside the Enterprise COBOL exemption in CONVENTIONS.md, so it is built to the 1974 standard, where a receiving group whose ODO object lies inside the group is sized from that object's value as it stands when the move begins - the count left behind by the record returned immediately before. The move consequently writes only as far as that count reached and leaves everything past it standing. Because the sort orders on BAN, then period, then section print order, then line sequence, the record returned immediately before is the neighbouring detail line of the same account in the same section of the same bill. The elements recovered at position twenty-nine and beyond are therefore well-formed packed decimal carrying a real rate element code, a real quantity, a real rate and real money - belonging to the line one place away. The failure does not present as corruption. It presents as a charge that has been billed twice.

Recompiling this same source under Enterprise COBOL changes the symptom and fixes nothing. That compiler sizes a receiving group of this shape at its maximum, so the move pads to 1,647 with X'40' and the elements past the cut come back as spaces, which the first arithmetic downstream turns into an S0C7. A rehost that recompiles and then chases the abend will find the truncation. A rehost that emulates the old compiler will keep shipping the duplicates.

Nothing on the record and nothing in the run says any of this happened. Every released line is returned and written, so the mandatory balancing equation in P8000-CONTROL holds exactly, CT-BAL-IND is written as 'B', and CABRPT01 passes the step. CT-HASH-AMOUNT is taken from WS-ACC-AMOUNT, which this program never accumulates, so the money hash is blind as well. BD-TOT-AMOUNT and BD-TOT-ROUNDED are both inside the 127-byte fixed portion, so the line total that CABBIL09 and CABBIL11 add up survives correctly - the invoice still adds up, and only the elements that are supposed to prove it are wrong. The comment above the SD still asserts that the image is wide enough for the longest record. That was true when it was written and stopped being true when the FDs were widened, and it is now the most convincing thing in the file.

Volume dependence, and why a small run proves nothing. Nothing at all happens below twenty-nine elements on a line, and a bill detail line only reaches twenty-nine elements when twenty-nine or more rated element records fold into a single BAN, period, section and line-sequence group in CABBIL02's P4100-ADD-ELEMENT. A SMOKE generation does not produce that shape, an ordinary random sample essentially never lands on it, and CABBIL02 opens a continuation line at the MAXELM limit, which caps how far the count can climb. The population has to be placed deliberately, or the run has to be large enough for the tail of the element-count distribution to reach past 28. A comparison that finds nothing here has established that the data carried no long lines. It has not established that the program is sound.

Provenance. This one was not planted. It was found during remediation, and it was created by the remediation: the FD clauses in this program were correctly widened from 1204 to 1647 when the declared record length of CABSBILL was closed out across the estate, and the SD in the same file was missed. That is exactly how a defect of this shape arises in production - a correct fix applied to the declarations that a search finds, and not applied to the one declaration that uses a different keyword. It is kept as a seeded defect because a synthetic estate that only contains defects somebody chose to write is not representative of the thing it is standing in for.
business_impact:
The invoice total is right and the evidence for it is fabricated. The line total survives the sort intact, so the summary page, the receivable and the estate's own account-level proof all agree; what changes is the detail printed underneath, where the widest lines on the bill carry charges lifted from the line next to them. Those lines are the largest, busiest accounts - a line reaches twenty-nine rate elements because the account generated enough switched access traffic in one section to need them - and the largest accounts are the ones with a settlement team that audits the bill element by element. A wholesale access dispute is argued at exactly that level of detail. A duplicated element on a switched access line is a dispute the counterparty wins on inspection, and the credit issued is only the visible part; the invisible part is what it costs to be the carrier whose bills cannot be reconciled to their own supporting detail. The exposure has been open since the FD widening went in, it is silent, and every control the estate owns reports the run as clean.

For a modernization programme the immediate cost is different and larger. A correct rewrite produces the correct detail, so it disagrees with the legacy on precisely the accounts that matter most, and the disagreement is on money that appears on a printed page a customer has already been sent. A programme that treats a parity failure as a defect in the transform will 'fix' the new system until it reproduces the duplication, sign it off as matching, and carry the defect forward into a platform that was going to be free of it.
correct_modernization_response:
Fix the estate first, and fix it in the right place. Widening SR-IMAGE and the SD to match the FD - 1,647 bytes of image, 1,675 bytes of sort record - closes the truncation and is the change to make if the internal sort stays. The better change is to stop imaging the record at all: the ordering step existed as its own job step until 1991 and was pulled inside the program to save a pass of the file, and an external sort of variable-length records has no fixed image to be too narrow. Whichever is chosen, add the rule that the truncation broke: wherever a variable-length record is moved into a fixed field, the two lengths are compared and a mismatch fails the step. A move that silently truncates is not an implementation detail, and one grep for fixed images of variable records will find the others.

Then understand what the target state does to the parity test, because this is the case the three-way verdict exists for. A Java or Python implementation holds the rate elements in a list on the invoice line object. There is no fixed intermediate buffer for them to be too long for, the sort is a sort of objects and not of a flattened image, and every element survives it. The target therefore produces the correct invoice detail - and fails parity against the legacy on every affected line, by an amount that is real money on a real bill. The verdict on that failure is DIVERGENT-BY-DESIGN. It is not a defect in the transform. The transform is being caught out for being right, and the single most damaging thing a programme can do here is take the red result at face value and reintroduce a fixed buffer to make it green.

So the sequence is: identify the affected population before cutover - every bill detail line whose element count exceeds twenty-eight, over as many historical cycles as are retained - and size it. Quantify the money on the duplicated elements and how long it has been going out, because that is a dispute-liability figure the business needs and not a technical one. Record the difference as a known and accepted change to the printed bill, signed off by whoever owns the invoice, before the new detail reaches a customer: the bill will visibly change for exactly the accounts most likely to compare it against last month's, and it will look like a regression to anyone who has not been told. Test the boundary explicitly at 28, 29 and 40 elements rather than trusting a volume run to reach it. And treat a lift-and-shift recompile as the trap it is - the same source under a modern compiler abends instead of duplicating, which is a change of symptom presented as a migration incident, with the underlying defect untouched.

One thing not to do: do not resolve the disagreement between the FD and the SD by narrowing the FD back to 1,204. That makes the two declarations consistent, makes the comparison green, and throws away eleven of the forty elements the copybook has always allowed.
